commentId.description:
CommentID is set only when the attachment is scoped to a comment.
JSON omits the field when nil so issue-level callers don't see it.

contentType.description:
ContentType is the MIME type the browser declared at upload time.
Re-validated against the deny-list before issuing the presigned URL.

filename.description:
Filename is the user-supplied original name (kept verbatim — used
in the Content-Disposition header on download).

id.description: ID is the attachment's own UUID (uuid.NewV7). Not the S3 key.

issueId.description: IssueID is the parent issue (always present).

sizeBytes.description:
SizeBytes is the file size in bytes (capped by config — see
Config.MaxSizeBytes).

status.description: Status is one of: pending | ready (closed set).

uploadedAt.description: UploadedAt is the row creation timestamp (UTC).

uploadedBy.description: UploadedBy is the user UUID (FK users.id, RESTRICT).

uploadedByUsername.description:
UploadedByUsername is the joined display name (best-effort —
nil if the user row was deleted or absent).

attachmentId.description:
AttachmentID is the row's UUID — pass it back to the confirm
endpoint after a successful upload.

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt is the absolute time the presigned URL stops working.
The browser should restart from upload-url if it fires later.

fields.description:
Fields is the form-data fields (key, policy, signature, etc.) the
browser must include in its multipart POST. Order does not matter.

maxSizeBytes.description:
MaxSizeBytes is the API-configured cap (informational — already
baked into the policy). UIs use it to decide whether to even
attempt the upload.

sizeBytes.description:
SizeBytes echoes the request value so the client doesn't have to
remember it for the confirm step.

url.description:
URL is the absolute S3 endpoint the browser should POST to
(rendered with S3_PUBLIC_URL when set).

parentIdCurrent.description:
sk-35: derived from the parent-child dep graph (first edge by
created_at); wire field renamed to parentIdCurrent so clients
don't assume it's a stored column.

closeLink.description:
CloseLink is PER ROW, not per call: one item may create the edge and
the next find it already there, in the same request. A per-call flag
would have to pick one of those answers and be wrong about the other.

closeOutcome.description:
CloseOutcome is the row's post-state outcome, same Go type and same
wire name as on the single acknowledgement (ack.go#ackRow).

issueId.description: IssueID and IssueTitle name the issue it rings on.

notifiedAt.description: NotifiedAt is when it last rang, RFC 3339; omitted before it did.

remindAt.description: RemindAt is when it rings, RFC 3339.

snoozeCount.description: SnoozeCount is how often it was snoozed.

id.description: ID is the blocker's hierarchical id.

status.description:
Status is the blocker's status: open, in_progress or deferred
(closed and standing targets never block).

authorStatus.description:
AuthorStatus — the author's person marks in the issue's space
(sk-674.18 T027): departed, or deleted with the pseudonym; absent
when nothing to mark or the author is not a user (an agent label).

mentions.description:
R4.3 — resolved @username mentions in `body`. See
IssueDetail.Mentions for the contract — same shape, scope here
is just the comment body. Always non-nil.

version.description:
sk-57 — edit/delete metadata.

Version is the optimistic-concurrency counter (starts at 1, bumped
on every edit). Edits pass expectedVersion; a mismatch surfaces as
ErrVersionConflict carrying the live value.

EditedAt is nil until the first edit; non-nil ⇒ the UI renders an
"edited" badge (tooltip = the edit timestamp). CreatedAt is never
rewritten.

DeletedAt is nil for live comments. When non-nil the row is a
tombstone: ListComments blanks Body and Mentions on read so deleted
text never reaches clients, but the slot remains in the thread.

counted.description:
Counted — the progress denominator: Total minus the visible dropped-out ones.
Unavailable ones stay in it, as today (INV-4).

done.description: Done — how many visible children are closed with the outcome "done". The numerator.

noWork.description:
NoWork — how many visible children are closed without work. They are not part of
the denominator; the chip prints them as a separate tail.

unavailable.description:
Unavailable counts children in projects the caller cannot see
(sk-291). They stay in Total and are absent from Closed, so a chip
with a non-zero Unavailable can never read as complete — which is
the honest answer, since whether those children are done is not
knowable from here. Not omitempty: a zero has to read as "counted,
and there are none" rather than as "not counted".

countedChildren.description:
CountedChildren — the progress denominator: TotalChildren minus the visible
dropped-out ones. Unavailable ones stay in the denominator, as today (INV-4):
it is not known whether they are done, and throwing them out would mean
asserting that they dropped out.

Its own name, not "total for progress", because TotalChildren next to it
keeps its previous meaning, and two different numbers must be named
differently.

doneChildren.description:
DoneChildren — how many children VISIBLE to the reader are closed with the outcome
"done". The numerator of progress. Unavailable children are not included
under any of their outcomes (INV-4).

noWorkChildren.description:
NoWorkChildren — how many VISIBLE children are closed without work (the outcome
differs from "done"). The number is counted by the SQL leg
`store.go#epicRollupFor` — the same as in the rows
(`store.go#epicSummaryNoWorkExpr`); the Go predicate
`close_outcome.go#IsNoWorkOutcome` writes the same rule as a whitelist,
but does not take part in the count. This is the "no work" tail next to
the ring; they are not part of the denominator.

acceptedAt.description:
AcceptedAt records when the current assignee explicitly accepted
the task. nil = "not yet accepted" (Inbox surfaces it as "needs
acceptance"). Reset to nil whenever the assignee changes; auto-
populated when the creator self-assigns. Phase 2 introduces
skein_accept + issue.accepted event for the explicit positive
transition.

acceptedBy.description:
AcceptedBy is the user UUID that produced the latest acceptance
(FK → users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL — the timestamp survives a
hard-delete of the user record). nil iff AcceptedAt is nil.

acceptedByUsername.description:
AcceptedByUsername is the username for AcceptedBy, joined via
LEFT JOIN users so a deleted accepter surfaces as nil. Optional
in the wire shape.

assigneeStatus.description:
AssigneeStatus / CreatedByStatus — the person marks of the assignee
and the author in the issue's space (sk-674.18 T027,
spaces/contract.go): departed, or deleted with the pseudonym. Absent
when there is nothing to mark, or when the assignee is free text.

blockers.description:
Blockers is the populated list backing IsBlocked: one entry per gating
blocker (neither closed nor standing, on the TO-side of an outgoing
blocks / waits-for edge) whose project is inside the reader's horizon,
ordered by id. Every entry is {id, title, status}. Always non-nil
(empty array when not blocked) so JS clients don't have to
special-case absence.

sk-423: the redacted form {id, redacted:true} that sk-421.1 put here
for a blocker outside the reader's horizon is gone — its mere presence
said that the hidden issue was not closed. Such edges are counted in
UnavailableBlockingLinks.

canForceUnlock.description:
CanForceUnlock — sk-674.18 T034 (US-16, K-28): the reader may release
another holder's claim on this issue (force_unlock: the project
owner, the space owner, the instance admin). Set by the card read
(GET …/issues/{id}) and the unlock action, which answer per reader;
absent on every other surface that returns a card.

closeOutcome.description:
CloseOutcome — the close outcome (sk-489, US-1): one of four values
from close_outcome.go, answering "how did it end", unlike the free
text of ClosedReason. It sits next to ClosedAt / ClosedReason because
it is a property of the same event — the close — while the wire name is taken from
the action (`closeOutcome`, like the "close" argument), not from the state.

Present if and only if the issue is closed (INV-1): an unclosed issue
has no key at all, a closed one always has it. Hence *string and
omitempty: the invariant is held by storage (the CHECK and the trigger of migration
000050), and the wire only repeats it — "no key" reads as "not
closed", and no value of the field can contradict that.

A client that receives a value outside the four prints it as is and does not
count it as done or as dropped out (INV-2) — it takes the numbers from
the server and does not derive them from the row.

dismissedByUsernames.description:
DismissedByUsernames is the username projection of
DismissedBy in matching order. Same missing-user semantics
as PreviousAssigneeUsernames.

epic.description:
sk-32: Epic rollup — populated only when issue.type == 'epic'.
nil for every other type (and JSON-omitted via omitempty). The
child set is sourced from the dependencies graph (parent-child
edges). sk-35 restored this as canonical.

EligibleForClose is true when TotalChildren > 0 AND
ClosedChildren == TotalChildren. Empty epics never become
eligible — they would be a false signal ("0 of 0 closed" is not
a meaningful "done" state).

inheritedComponentIds.description:
InheritedComponentIDs is the transient "echo what happened on
this call" channel populated exclusively by CreateIssue when the
caller omitted componentIds AND a parent was supplied AND the
parent (same project) had components attached. The store copies
the parent's set into ComponentIDs at INSERT time and mirrors
the inherited slice here so the caller can surface a warning
("inherited foo, bar from parent — override via skein_update if
wrong"). GetIssue / Patch / List paths never populate this field;
omitempty keeps it absent on every non-create read.

isBlocked.description:
IsBlocked is the derived "this issue is blocked" flag (sk-31), FOR THE
READER (sk-423): true when at least one outgoing blocks / waits-for
edge points at a target issue whose status is neither 'closed' nor
'standing' AND whose project is inside the reader's horizon. A blocker
outside the horizon never makes this true — it is reported as a link in
UnavailableBlockingLinks instead. Agents never write it and the UI never
caches it across edge mutations.

INV-11 (sk-421.1, restated by sk-423): on the detail it is DERIVED FROM
Blockers of the same response — true if and only if Blockers is
non-empty — so the flag and the list always describe one state of the
graph.

lockedByUsername.description:
LockedByUsername is the username of the user who PERFORMED the claim
that holds the lock now (sk-421.1, US-15) — derived on read from that
claim's issue.claimed event, never stored. Present only while the
issue is locked AND that event is found; absent (not empty) otherwise,
so it disappears with the lock on unclaim, close, auto-release or a
forced release. For an admin who claimed on behalf of another user it
is the admin, not the assignee. A request that does not change the
lock cannot change it, whichever session it presents. LockedBy keeps
the MCP session id; this field never repeats it.

mentions.description:
R4.3 — resolved @username mentions across description / notes /
acceptance_criteria / design. Frontend renderer substitutes the
<UserMention> component for `@username` matches whose username is
in this list; unresolved `@foo` stays plain text. Always non-nil
(`[]` rather than `null`) so JS clients don't have to special-
case absence.

parentIdCurrent.description:
ParentID is the current parent id derived from the dependencies
graph (parent-child edge, first by created_at). Wire field is
`parentIdCurrent` since sk-35 — the `issues.parent_id` column is
frozen for backward-compat reads but no longer authoritative.
Absent when the parent's project is not visible to the reader
(sk-674.18 T009).

previousAssigneeUsernames.description:
PreviousAssigneeUsernames is the username projection of
PreviousAssignees in matching order. Surfaced so the UI can
render a human-readable delegation chain without an extra
per-uuid resolve. Missing users (deleted accounts) project
as empty strings — the UI should treat empty slots as
"unknown" and skip them when rendering.

previousAssignees.description:
sk-34 — delegation chain. PreviousAssignees lists every user UUID
that was ever this issue's assignee (with no duplicates), append-
ordered by reassignment timestamp. PatchIssue's assignee-change
branch appends the old assignee on each reassign and prunes the
new assignee when they "come back" (the array tracks PAST
assignees only — the current assignee is never present).

DismissedBy lists users who explicitly opted out of this issue's
Delegated lens via the "Drop from Delegated" affordance
(skein_drop_delegated MCP tool / POST /issues/{id}/dismiss). Sticky
— entries clear only when the user becomes the current assignee
again. The Delegated lens predicate is:

  created_by = me
  OR (me ∈ previous_assignees
      AND me ∉ dismissed_by
      AND assignee != me)

Both arrays are wire-omitempty — older clients that don't know the
fields simply see nothing extra. JSON shape is always []uuid (empty
arrays normalise to absence via omitempty + nil slice).

reviewRequired.description:
--- sk-303.14, contract C1 — the author's private
bookkeeping (INV-2, SC-028). ---

Three review-mechanic fields. They land on the card ONLY when the
caller is the issue author (issues.CreatedBy), and they are filled
in EXACTLY one place — applyReviewVisibility (review_visibility.go).
Other readers have no keys in the object at all: not `null`, not
`false`, not zero — absence, because "no field" and "no mark" must
be indistinguishable to the assignee.

Hence pointers and `omitempty` on all three, including the flag: on
a flat bool `omitempty` strips `false` and keeps `true`, which would
disclose exactly half the state; a nil pointer removes the key at
any value, and a non-nil pointer to false gives
`"reviewRequired":false` to the author.

There is NO username projection of the mark author here on purpose:
contract C1 is three fields, and only the issue author may set the
mark (INV-4), so reviewedBy is always equal to createdBy, whose
name is already on the card as createdByUsername. A fourth key
would add no information and would widen the contract the frontend
consumes.

rowSeq.description:
RowSeq is the row freshness order of the issue (sk-622.21, US-15,
decision K16) — the same value and the same rule as
[IssueSummary.RowSeq]: an open card takes a phase-2 event row
([NeutralRow]) only if the row's RowSeq is greater than this one.

Read in ONE statement with the issue's own columns AND the card's
labels and components (issueRowSelect, rowComponentsLabelsCols —
decision R26 item 2): the card is one snapshot, exactly the state its
RowSeq names. A separate later read of the labels could show labels
newer than RowSeq, and an intermediate event row with a greater RowSeq
would then roll them back under the strict-greater rule. Zero (key absent) — the issue row has not been written
since the phase-2 rollout (migration 000064), order unknown; see
[IssueSummary.RowSeq].

spaceId.description:
SpaceID is the short id of the space of the issue's project
(sk-674.18 T032), not of its id prefix.

unavailableBlockingLinks.description:
UnavailableBlockingLinks is the number of outgoing blocks / waits-for
edges of this issue whose target lives in a project outside the
reader's horizon — counted WHATEVER the target's status, closed and
standing included (sk-423). It is the fact of the link, never a claim
that the link blocks: it does not depend on the hidden issue's status,
so it cannot reveal it (the same rule as depsCounts' `unavailable`
bucket and epic.unavailableChildren). Always present; 0 when there is
none, and always 0 for a reader who sees every project.

Readiness (skein_ready) keeps counting every blocker, so an issue with
isBlocked=false and UnavailableBlockingLinks > 0 may be absent from the
ready list: whether such a link still blocks is not knowable from here.

acceptedAt.description:
AcceptedAt mirrors IssueDetail.AcceptedAt but at the summary
level so the Inbox / list views can render the "needs acceptance"
chip without round-tripping for the full detail. AcceptedBy /
AcceptedByUsername are NOT carried on the summary — only needed
when the user opens the issue.

assigneeStatus.description:
AssigneeStatus / CreatedByStatus — the person marks of the assignee
and the author in the issue's space (sk-674.18 T027,
spaces/contract.go): departed, or deleted with the pseudonym. Absent
when there is nothing to mark, or when the assignee is free text.

closeOutcome.description:
CloseOutcome mirrors IssueDetail.CloseOutcome on the row (sk-489,
US-1): the same key, the same Go type, the same rule "present exactly for
a closed one" (INV-1). One type on the card and on the row — so that
the consumer does not have to know which surface answered.

In MCP rows the field is "selectable, not default": the default set
does not contain it, and it arrives only on an explicit `fields`
(`mcp/tools/issuerow.go`, the classification is in its guard test).
The task column and the board do not show the field — it is on the wire, and
it has two surfaces: the card and the rows of the epic section.

epicProgress.description:
EpicProgress carries the cheap (closed,total) child-count pair on
epic rows so the task list can render inline progress without a
per-row IssueDetail fetch. nil/omitted on every non-epic row.
Slice 2 of sk-32 — children sourced from the dependencies graph
(parent-child edges). sk-35 restored this as canonical.

iAssigned.description:
IAssigned is true when the caller created the issue and assigned it
to someone else. Used by the UI to highlight "tasks I delegated" in
default mode. Computed in ListIssues based on the caller's user id
(passed via ListIssuesArgs.Caller); absent (false) for unauthenticated
callers and for issues the caller is also the assignee of (no point
highlighting your own work). Phase 2 ui-redesign — B5.

isBlocked.description:
IsBlocked is the derived "this issue is blocked" flag (sk-31), for
the reader (sk-423: only blockers inside the reader's horizon count) —
EXISTS over the dep graph at SELECT time (isBlockedExprFor). List
endpoints surface it on every row so cards can render the [blocked]
chip without a per-row Get round-trip. The detail's
IssueDetail.IsBlocked is no longer this expression: since sk-421.1 it
is derived from the detail's own blockers list (non-empty ⇔ blocked),
over the same set of blocking statuses.

parentIdCurrent.description:
sk-35: derived from the parent-child dep graph (first edge by
created_at). Wire field is `parentIdCurrent` — see IssueDetail
for the full rationale; absent when the reader cannot see the
parent (sk-674.18 T009).

rowSeq.description:
RowSeq is the row freshness order (sk-622.21, US-15, decision K16):
the value of the issues row's freshness sequence after the last
committed change of ANY of its columns — including writes that do not
bump Version (label add/remove, component replace). For one issue a
greater RowSeq is always a later committed state; values of different
issues are not comparable in any useful way. It is the same order the
phase-2 event row ([NeutralRow.RowSeq]) carries, so a client compares
the two directly — see [NeutralRow] for the substitution rule.

Populated on every REST list, tree and card read since migration
000064 (T026): the column `issues.row_seq` is NOT NULL and a trigger
assigns the next value of the global sequence on every INSERT and
UPDATE of the issue row, after the row lock is taken — so the order of
RowSeq for one issue is the order of its commits. Writes that touch
only side tables (labels, components, the child's parent-child edge —
dependencies/store.go#touchChildRow) also UPDATE the issue row and
therefore move it. Every REST read takes a row's labels and component
ids in the SAME statement as its RowSeq (store.go#rowComponentsLabelsCols,
decision R26 item 2), so a row is one snapshot: its fields are exactly
the state its RowSeq names, never newer or older.

Zero means "order unknown", and on the wire it is the ABSENT key
(`omitempty`, deliberately: absent ≡ 0, a client reads a missing
`rowSeq` as 0). Two sources of zero:
  - the issue row has not been written since the phase-2 rollout:
    migration 000064 adds the column without a backfill (decision R26,
    no table rewrite), so untouched rows read 0 until their next write;
  - a carrier that does not read the column (a redacted `<hidden>`
    tree stub, the Ready surface).
Any write after the rollout gives the row a positive value, and an
event row is read from the issue's current state, so an event row
with a positive RowSeq is always fresher than a shown zero; an event
older than a REST row showing zero cannot exist. An event row with
zero carries the same state as a shown zero row. The value fits a
JSON number exactly (a global sequence stays far below 2^53).

spaceId.description:
SpaceID is the short id of the space of the issue's project
(sk-674.18 T032), not of its id prefix.

status.description:
Status — the mentioned person's marks in the issue's space
(sk-674.18 T027): deleted with the pseudonym; absent when nothing
to mark. A person outside the space does not resolve at all (INV-9).

departed.description:
Departed — the person has left the space of this context (the
issue's project); shown greyed. Never set together with Deleted.

pseudonym.description:
Pseudonym — the stable alias of a deleted account
(users.pseudonym, `deleted-<8hex>`); absent otherwise.

marked.description:
Marked is how many notifications this call flipped from unread to
read, counted in notification rows. Rows already read are not
counted, so a repeated call answers 0. It may exceed the drop of the
Watching badge, which counts only unread rows inside the window.

actor.description:
Actor is who caused the event — resolved in the same query, so a
client never has to look a username up per row. A system-caused
event has no userId.

actorSessionId.description:
ActorSessionID carries the originating event's actor_session_id and is
populated ONLY on the agent monitor-poll path (PollForMonitor). It lets
the monitor runner / agent skip its own echo — an event whose
actorSessionId equals the agent's current MCP session (sk-164 US-2,
INV-2, reader-side self-skip).

`omitempty` is load-bearing: NotificationDTO is shared with the human
inbox (ListInbox / me), where this field stays nil and
must NOT surface as `actorSessionId:null` — that inert null would change
the human inbox JSON and break "human path unchanged" (INV-5 / SC-004;
spec Changelog 2026-07-20). Present only when the event carried a
non-empty actor_session_id; absent otherwise (nil → omitempty). The
reader treats absent ≡ empty session ≡ "not mine".

archivedAt.description:
ArchivedAt is when the recipient archived the row; absent while it
is not archived. An archived row is excluded from every scope but
`archived`.

closeOutcome.description:
CloseOutcome — the outcome of closing the issue the row is about (sk-489, US-3,
the "Notifications" contract). Present on issue.status_changed rows
that report a transition to "closed", and only when the outcome is known.

This is a field of the short summary in the API response, not text: the UI prints
the outcome in the push title and in the feed row from Summary, and from here it is taken
by whoever needs a machine-distinguishable value rather than a phrase.

For issue.outcome_changed the outcome change is carried by the regular Field / OldValue /
NewValue (field = "closeOutcome"), and duplicating it here is pointless —
"was → became" is a pair, not a single value.

omitempty is mandatory: the field is empty on the vast majority of rows
(comments, mentions, assignments), and an inert `closeOutcome:null`
would change the JSON of the inbox on every one of them.

commentId.description:
CommentID / BodyPreview / Truncated are monitor-only enrichment for
comment-entity events on the agent poll path (sk-242.1 US-1/2, FR-002,
INV-5). Filled ONLY by PollForMonitor; human materialization paths
(ListInbox / watching recent / MCP
skein_notifications(action="inbox")) leave
them nil so omitempty keeps the human JSON byte-stable.

Wire (comment.created monitor items):
  - commentId: event entity UUID string when parseable; parallel to
    Entity (which re-points comment→issue, INV-9).
  - bodyPreview: live comments.body snapshot at first delivery, rune-
    truncated to BodyPreviewMaxRunes (INV-2). *string so nil = absent
    and non-nil "" = present empty string (string omitempty would drop "").
  - truncated: non-nil true only when live body exceeded the rune cap;
    absent (nil) when ≤ cap, soft-deleted, orphan, or non-comment.
Soft-deleted / orphan / unparseable: commentId may still be present;
bodyPreview and truncated stay nil (INV-4 — deleted text never on poll).

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the row was minted for this recipient (UTC).

entity.description:
Entity is what the row is about, already re-pointed to the thing a
client can open: for a comment event this is the ISSUE the comment
is on, not the comment.

field.description:
Field, OldValue and NewValue come straight off the events row — for
status_changed a client renders "open → in_progress" without
parsing the raw payload. Field names WHAT changed; the two values
are its before and after, and either may be absent when the event
has no such side (a creation has no old value). Their JSON type
follows the field, so they are not always strings.

id.description:
ID is the row's identifier and the paging key: pages run in
DESCENDING id, and the lowest id of a page is what comes back as
nextCursor. On the agent monitor-poll path this is the EVENT id
instead (that path reads the audit log, not the inbox), so the two
id namespaces are not interchangeable across the two endpoints.

mentionContext.description:
MentionContext is a ~120-character snippet of the body where the
mention happened (sk-38). Pre-trimmed around the first
`@<caller-username>` occurrence so the UI can render a meaningful
preview ("...we should loop in @admin on this before the merge...").
Only populated for mention-typed notifications (comment.mention /
issue.mention). Wire-omitempty — non-mention rows lack the field.

readAt.description:
ReadAt is when the recipient marked the row read; absent while it
is unread. Absent and null are the same statement here: the field
is omitted, never sent as null.

spaceId.description:
SpaceID is the short id of the space of the row's project (sk-674.18
T029, spaces/contract.go: Inbox, Mentions, Watching rows). Absent on
the agent monitor-poll path and on a row without a project.

summary.description:
Summary is the ready-to-render one-line phrase for the row, built
server-side so every surface words the same event identically.

type.description:
Type is the event type the row reports, e.g. issue.status_changed,
comment.created, comment.mention. The enumerated set is served by
GET /api/v1/notification-event-types rather than being frozen here.

eventTypes.description:
EventTypes mirrors project_watchers.event_types. nil means "all
notifiable types"; an explicit list is a strict whitelist.

departed.description:
Departed — the person has left the space of this context (the
issue's project); shown greyed. Never set together with Deleted.

pseudonym.description:
Pseudonym — the stable alias of a deleted account
(users.pseudonym, `deleted-<8hex>`); absent otherwise.

myOutboxOpenCount.description:
MyOutbox{Open,InProgress,Blocked}Count narrow component issue
aggregates to "issues the caller created AND delegated to someone
else" — created_by = caller AND assignee IS NOT NULL AND
LOWER(assignee) <> LOWER(callerUsername).

NOTE: the component path intentionally uses this narrower
created_by-only predicate (unlike ProjectListItem.MyOutbox*, which
includes the sk-34 previous_assignees / dismissed_by chain). Aligning
components to the full Delegated lens is a separate follow-up.
ListComponents fills these only when the caller is known; Get /
Patch / Create leave them at zero.

myOutboxStandingCount.description:
MyOutboxStandingCount is the outbox-scoped standing aggregate — the
"Standing" pill under outboxMode. Same created_by-only Delegated
predicate as MyOutboxOpenCount, narrowed to status='standing'.

onMeOpenCount.description:
OnMe{Open,InProgress,Blocked}Count are the "On me" lens
counterparts (sk-30): per-status aggregates narrowed to "issues
assigned to the caller by someone else that the caller has
accepted" — LOWER(assignee) = LOWER(callerUsername) AND
created_by <> caller AND accepted_at IS NOT NULL. Same fill rules
as MyOutbox*.

openCount.description:
OpenCount / InProgressCount / BlockedCount are populated by
ListComponents via a LEFT JOIN against issue_components + issues.
Get / Patch / Create paths leave them at zero (the caller doesn't
render right-aligned counts in those flows).

sk-423: as on the project row, «blocked» here and in every
*BlockedCount below (open / in_progress being its disjoint
complement) counts only blockers in projects the CALLER can see.

standingCount.description:
StandingCount is the count of standing (perpetual-obligation) issues
attached to the component. Its OWN pill (sk-118.8, decision #4):
standing is EXCLUDED from OpenCount / InProgressCount / BlockedCount
(which route through status.ActiveWork) and reported here. Filled only
by ListComponents; Get / Patch / Create leave it zero.

departed.description:
Departed — the person has left the space of this context (the
issue's project); shown greyed. Never set together with Deleted.

pseudonym.description:
Pseudonym — the stable alias of a deleted account
(users.pseudonym, `deleted-<8hex>`); absent otherwise.

spaceId.description:
SpaceID is the short id of the project's space (sk-674.18, never
null since T024).

visibility.description:
Visibility is "space" (every participant of the space sees it) or
"members" (only its members and the space owner).

componentsCount.description:
ComponentsCount is the number of NON-archived components of the
project (sk-551.53) — the same figure GET /projects/{id} reports as
ProjectDTO.ComponentsCount; archived components are not counted. A
project with no active component reports 0. It is a property of the
project, not of the caller's issues, so it is identical under every
lens and toggle (no myOutbox / onMe variant). Lets the shell decide
whether a project row can expand into components without a per-row
request.

epicsEligibleCount.description:
EpicsEligibleCount is the number of epic-typed, non-closed issues
in this project whose child set is non-empty AND every child is
closed — i.e. epics the UI should surface as "ready to close"
(sk-32). Empty epics never qualify. Children sourced from the
dependencies graph (parent-child edges). sk-35 restored this as
canonical. Computed in the same SELECT as the row-level status
counters so we don't pay a second round-trip.

myOutboxOpenCount.description:
MyOutbox{Open,InProgress,Blocked}Count are the same per-status
aggregates scoped to the caller's Delegated (outbox) lens (sk-34):

	(created_by = caller
	  AND assignee IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(assignee) <> LOWER(callerUsername))
	OR (caller = ANY(previous_assignees)
	  AND NOT caller = ANY(dismissed_by)
	  AND assignee IS NOT NULL AND LOWER(assignee) <> LOWER(callerUsername))

Powers the shell's `My-assigned mode` (outboxMode) header toggle so
every row count flips to the caller's delegated scope when ON.
Filled only when the caller identity is known (CallerID != uuid.Nil);
otherwise stays at zero.

myOutboxStandingCount.description:
MyOutboxStandingCount is the outbox-scoped standing aggregate — the
"Standing" pill under the `My-assigned mode` (outboxMode) toggle.
Same Delegated predicate as MyOutboxOpenCount, narrowed to
status='standing'. Honors the outboxMode invariant (CLAUDE.md).

onMeOpenCount.description:
OnMe{Open,InProgress,Blocked}Count are the "On me" lens
counterparts (sk-30): per-status aggregates narrowed to "issues
assigned to the caller by SOMEONE ELSE that the caller has already
accepted" — LOWER(assignee) = LOWER(callerUsername) AND
created_by <> caller AND accepted_at IS NOT NULL. Powers the
header "On me" toggle so every row count flips to the caller's
active-work scope when ON. Filled only when the caller identity
is known; collapses to zero otherwise.

openCount.description:
OpenCount / InProgressCount / BlockedCount are aggregated in the
same SELECT as the row itself via LEFT JOIN issues + COUNT(*)
FILTER. Issues have no archived_at — `status = 'closed'` is the
terminal state, so the filters key off status alone.

sk-423: «blocked» here — and in every *BlockedCount below, with the
open / in_progress counts as its disjoint complement — means blocked
by a blocks / waits-for target that gates readiness AND lives in a
project the CALLER can see (authz.ReaderBlockedExpr). An issue
blocked only from outside the caller's horizon counts as open /
in_progress: counting it as blocked would reveal whether that hidden
blocker is closed. Readiness (skein_ready) still counts every blocker.

spaceId.description: SpaceID is the short id of the project's space (sk-674.18 T024).

standingCount.description:
StandingCount is the count of standing (perpetual-obligation) issues
on the project row. Surfaced as its OWN pill (sk-118.8, decision #4):
standing is EXCLUDED from OpenCount / InProgressCount / BlockedCount
(which route through status.ActiveWork) and reported here so the board
renders a distinct "Standing" pill rather than folding it into open.

done.description:
Done / NoWork split Closed by the CLOSE OUTCOME (sk-494, on the rule
sk-489 normalised): "closed" does not equal "done". Done counts closed
issues whose outcome is `done`; NoWork counts the other three
outcomes — "won't do", "duplicate", "superseded" — the ones the
spec calls "closed without work".

⚠ Closed KEEPS ITS MEANING — it is still every closed issue, at any
outcome (sk-489 INV-3, and the spec's "all breakdowns BY STATUS
stay unchanged": this block is a status breakdown). The split
is ADDED beside it, so `Done + NoWork = Closed` is an identity that
holds on the wire at any data — that identity is what a reader uses
to tell «this api knows outcomes» from «it does not», and it is what
`close_outcome_stats_test.go#TestGetProjectWithStats_CloseOutcomeSplit`
asserts.

Why NoWork is the leg SQL counts and Done is derived in Go: exactly
as in `issues/store.go#epicSummaryNoWorkExpr`, one correlated leg
cannot drift from Closed the way two independent spellings of
«visible» and «closed» could. Same predicate, same spelling:
`status = 'closed' AND close_outcome <> 'done'`.

Both are project-wide, like every other count here except MyAssigned
/ MyCreated — the issue's own outcome is not horizon-dependent, and
a project the caller can read they can read whole.

open.description:
Open / InProgress / Blocked are disjoint; «blocked» counts only
blockers in projects the caller can see (sk-423, the same rule as
ProjectListItem.BlockedCount).

standingCount.description:
Standing is the count of perpetual-obligation issues (status='standing')
in the project. It is surfaced as its OWN aggregate (sk-118.8,
decision #4): standing issues are EXCLUDED from Open / InProgress /
Blocked / MyAssigned (which all route through status.ActiveWork) and
reported here instead, so the board can render a distinct "Standing"
pill rather than folding standing into open work.

issueId.description: IssueID is the issue the comment belongs to.

issue.description:
Issue is the OTHER end of the edge from the request perspective —
for outgoing lists Issue == to-side; for incoming, Issue == from-side.
Always non-nil unless Redacted is true.

redacted.description:
Redacted marks an edge whose other end the caller cannot see: no
Issue, and that end's id (ToID outgoing, FromID incoming) is a
synthetic "hidden-N" token, never the real id (sk-674.18 T009).

fromId.description: FromID, ToID and Type name the edge that was removed.

notFound.description: NotFound are the hashes the issue had no link with.

acceptedAt.description:
AcceptedAt records when the current assignee explicitly accepted
the task. nil = "not yet accepted" (Inbox surfaces it as "needs
acceptance"). Reset to nil whenever the assignee changes; auto-
populated when the creator self-assigns. Phase 2 introduces
skein_accept + issue.accepted event for the explicit positive
transition.

acceptedBy.description:
AcceptedBy is the user UUID that produced the latest acceptance
(FK → users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL — the timestamp survives a
hard-delete of the user record). nil iff AcceptedAt is nil.

acceptedByUsername.description:
AcceptedByUsername is the username for AcceptedBy, joined via
LEFT JOIN users so a deleted accepter surfaces as nil. Optional
in the wire shape.

assigneeStatus.description:
AssigneeStatus / CreatedByStatus — the person marks of the assignee
and the author in the issue's space (sk-674.18 T027,
spaces/contract.go): departed, or deleted with the pseudonym. Absent
when there is nothing to mark, or when the assignee is free text.

blockers.description:
Blockers is the populated list backing IsBlocked: one entry per gating
blocker (neither closed nor standing, on the TO-side of an outgoing
blocks / waits-for edge) whose project is inside the reader's horizon,
ordered by id. Every entry is {id, title, status}. Always non-nil
(empty array when not blocked) so JS clients don't have to
special-case absence.

sk-423: the redacted form {id, redacted:true} that sk-421.1 put here
for a blocker outside the reader's horizon is gone — its mere presence
said that the hidden issue was not closed. Such edges are counted in
UnavailableBlockingLinks.

canForceUnlock.description:
CanForceUnlock — sk-674.18 T034 (US-16, K-28): the reader may release
another holder's claim on this issue (force_unlock: the project
owner, the space owner, the instance admin). Set by the card read
(GET …/issues/{id}) and the unlock action, which answer per reader;
absent on every other surface that returns a card.

children.description: Children are the children created with the epic.

closeOutcome.description:
CloseOutcome — the close outcome (sk-489, US-1): one of four values
from close_outcome.go, answering "how did it end", unlike the free
text of ClosedReason. It sits next to ClosedAt / ClosedReason because
it is a property of the same event — the close — while the wire name is taken from
the action (`closeOutcome`, like the "close" argument), not from the state.

Present if and only if the issue is closed (INV-1): an unclosed issue
has no key at all, a closed one always has it. Hence *string and
omitempty: the invariant is held by storage (the CHECK and the trigger of migration
000050), and the wire only repeats it — "no key" reads as "not
closed", and no value of the field can contradict that.

A client that receives a value outside the four prints it as is and does not
count it as done or as dropped out (INV-2) — it takes the numbers from
the server and does not derive them from the row.

dismissedByUsernames.description:
DismissedByUsernames is the username projection of
DismissedBy in matching order. Same missing-user semantics
as PreviousAssigneeUsernames.

epic.description:
sk-32: Epic rollup — populated only when issue.type == 'epic'.
nil for every other type (and JSON-omitted via omitempty). The
child set is sourced from the dependencies graph (parent-child
edges). sk-35 restored this as canonical.

EligibleForClose is true when TotalChildren > 0 AND
ClosedChildren == TotalChildren. Empty epics never become
eligible — they would be a false signal ("0 of 0 closed" is not
a meaningful "done" state).

inheritedComponentIds.description:
InheritedComponentIDs is the transient "echo what happened on
this call" channel populated exclusively by CreateIssue when the
caller omitted componentIds AND a parent was supplied AND the
parent (same project) had components attached. The store copies
the parent's set into ComponentIDs at INSERT time and mirrors
the inherited slice here so the caller can surface a warning
("inherited foo, bar from parent — override via skein_update if
wrong"). GetIssue / Patch / List paths never populate this field;
omitempty keeps it absent on every non-create read.

isBlocked.description:
IsBlocked is the derived "this issue is blocked" flag (sk-31), FOR THE
READER (sk-423): true when at least one outgoing blocks / waits-for
edge points at a target issue whose status is neither 'closed' nor
'standing' AND whose project is inside the reader's horizon. A blocker
outside the horizon never makes this true — it is reported as a link in
UnavailableBlockingLinks instead. Agents never write it and the UI never
caches it across edge mutations.

INV-11 (sk-421.1, restated by sk-423): on the detail it is DERIVED FROM
Blockers of the same response — true if and only if Blockers is
non-empty — so the flag and the list always describe one state of the
graph.

lockedByUsername.description:
LockedByUsername is the username of the user who PERFORMED the claim
that holds the lock now (sk-421.1, US-15) — derived on read from that
claim's issue.claimed event, never stored. Present only while the
issue is locked AND that event is found; absent (not empty) otherwise,
so it disappears with the lock on unclaim, close, auto-release or a
forced release. For an admin who claimed on behalf of another user it
is the admin, not the assignee. A request that does not change the
lock cannot change it, whichever session it presents. LockedBy keeps
the MCP session id; this field never repeats it.

mentions.description:
R4.3 — resolved @username mentions across description / notes /
acceptance_criteria / design. Frontend renderer substitutes the
<UserMention> component for `@username` matches whose username is
in this list; unresolved `@foo` stays plain text. Always non-nil
(`[]` rather than `null`) so JS clients don't have to special-
case absence.

parentIdCurrent.description:
ParentID is the current parent id derived from the dependencies
graph (parent-child edge, first by created_at). Wire field is
`parentIdCurrent` since sk-35 — the `issues.parent_id` column is
frozen for backward-compat reads but no longer authoritative.
Absent when the parent's project is not visible to the reader
(sk-674.18 T009).

previousAssigneeUsernames.description:
PreviousAssigneeUsernames is the username projection of
PreviousAssignees in matching order. Surfaced so the UI can
render a human-readable delegation chain without an extra
per-uuid resolve. Missing users (deleted accounts) project
as empty strings — the UI should treat empty slots as
"unknown" and skip them when rendering.

previousAssignees.description:
sk-34 — delegation chain. PreviousAssignees lists every user UUID
that was ever this issue's assignee (with no duplicates), append-
ordered by reassignment timestamp. PatchIssue's assignee-change
branch appends the old assignee on each reassign and prunes the
new assignee when they "come back" (the array tracks PAST
assignees only — the current assignee is never present).

DismissedBy lists users who explicitly opted out of this issue's
Delegated lens via the "Drop from Delegated" affordance
(skein_drop_delegated MCP tool / POST /issues/{id}/dismiss). Sticky
— entries clear only when the user becomes the current assignee
again. The Delegated lens predicate is:

  created_by = me
  OR (me ∈ previous_assignees
      AND me ∉ dismissed_by
      AND assignee != me)

Both arrays are wire-omitempty — older clients that don't know the
fields simply see nothing extra. JSON shape is always []uuid (empty
arrays normalise to absence via omitempty + nil slice).

reviewRequired.description:
--- sk-303.14, contract C1 — the author's private
bookkeeping (INV-2, SC-028). ---

Three review-mechanic fields. They land on the card ONLY when the
caller is the issue author (issues.CreatedBy), and they are filled
in EXACTLY one place — applyReviewVisibility (review_visibility.go).
Other readers have no keys in the object at all: not `null`, not
`false`, not zero — absence, because "no field" and "no mark" must
be indistinguishable to the assignee.

Hence pointers and `omitempty` on all three, including the flag: on
a flat bool `omitempty` strips `false` and keeps `true`, which would
disclose exactly half the state; a nil pointer removes the key at
any value, and a non-nil pointer to false gives
`"reviewRequired":false` to the author.

There is NO username projection of the mark author here on purpose:
contract C1 is three fields, and only the issue author may set the
mark (INV-4), so reviewedBy is always equal to createdBy, whose
name is already on the card as createdByUsername. A fourth key
would add no information and would widen the contract the frontend
consumes.

rowSeq.description:
RowSeq is the row freshness order of the issue (sk-622.21, US-15,
decision K16) — the same value and the same rule as
[IssueSummary.RowSeq]: an open card takes a phase-2 event row
([NeutralRow]) only if the row's RowSeq is greater than this one.

Read in ONE statement with the issue's own columns AND the card's
labels and components (issueRowSelect, rowComponentsLabelsCols —
decision R26 item 2): the card is one snapshot, exactly the state its
RowSeq names. A separate later read of the labels could show labels
newer than RowSeq, and an intermediate event row with a greater RowSeq
would then roll them back under the strict-greater rule. Zero (key absent) — the issue row has not been written
since the phase-2 rollout (migration 000064), order unknown; see
[IssueSummary.RowSeq].

SpaceID is the short id of the space of the issue's project
(sk-674.18 T032), not of its id prefix.

unavailableBlockingLinks.description:
UnavailableBlockingLinks is the number of outgoing blocks / waits-for
edges of this issue whose target lives in a project outside the
reader's horizon — counted WHATEVER the target's status, closed and
standing included (sk-423). It is the fact of the link, never a claim
that the link blocks: it does not depend on the hidden issue's status,
so it cannot reveal it (the same rule as depsCounts' `unavailable`
bucket and epic.unavailableChildren). Always present; 0 when there is
none, and always 0 for a reader who sees every project.

Readiness (skein_ready) keeps counting every blocker, so an issue with
isBlocked=false and UnavailableBlockingLinks > 0 may be absent from the
ready list: whether such a link still blocks is not knowable from here.

Soft-deletes the comment of the path — the same operation as the MCP tool skein_comment_delete: the row stays in the thread as a tombstone with its body blanked on read. The author deletes his own comment with write; another's needs the owner's role delete_any_comment on the project (the project owner, the space owner, the instance admin), else 403 forbidden. Deleting a deleted comment succeeds again without a change. A comment of a project out of reach answers as a missing one, before authorship is looked at.

Only the author edits a comment; another user, an owner or an admin included, gets 403 forbidden. If-Match is required: the version of the comment (its ETag); a stale one answers 412 version_conflict with the current version and nothing is written. A deleted comment is not edited (422 validation_error, comment_deleted). The comment keeps its author kind; kind is optional and checked. A comment of a project out of reach answers as a missing one, before authorship is looked at.

Side effects: comment.edited; mentions added by the edit are resolved and notified.

Creates a project in a space; the key's owner becomes its owner. The same operation as the MCP tool skein_project_create:
1. The name and the optional prefix, id mode, description, aliases and repositories are validated; an omitted prefix is the first free one derived from the name.
2. The space is the one named, or the only space the owner may create projects in (several — space_required with their list). A key limited to spaces creates only inside them; a key limited to projects cannot create one (insufficient_scope, requiredScope).
3. In one transaction, under the space's lock: the owner must still take part in the space, the space's project quota must allow one more, the prefix must be free (no project, deleted project, alias or reserved word holds it), the name free in the space, every alias free; then the project, the owner's membership, the members of a space-visible project and the aliases and repositories are written, with the project.created event. Any refusal writes nothing.

Side effects: project.created event; every member of the space who sees the project gains it in live updates. The Location header names the new project.

post.description:
Creates an issue in the project of the path — the same operation as the MCP tool skein_create:
1. The fields are checked; the owner must be able to write in the project (and to assign, when assignee is given).
2. Unless force or duplicateOf, the duplicate gate looks for similar issues of the project: found — nothing is created, the answer is 422 duplicate_suspected with the candidates (duplicates; degraded when only the lexical check ran). Repeat with force=true to create anyway, or with duplicateOf to create it as a duplicate.
3. One transaction writes the issue, its components, labels, the inline dependencies (each refusal rolls everything back) and, with duplicateOf, the duplicates edge.

Without kind the issue's source is api; kind directed and autonomous give the agent's sources, with the same side effects as in MCP (the author's auto-watch, the notification rules, the default assignee). Accepts Idempotency-Key: a repeat within 24 h answers the first outcome without creating anything. Side effects: issue.created and the events of the edges; notifications of the assignee and the watchers. The Location header names the issue, ETag is its version.
